title: Limit public authentication requests
responsibility: Count selected POST requests in a per-address, per-route one-minute database window.

inputs.name: hubRateLimit.input
inputs.type: { request: Request; db?: D1Database; secret?: string; ip?: string; now?: number; }
inputs.description: The request, whose method must be POST and whose URL pathname must be one of the nine listed routes before any counting happens, plus optional db (the D1 database holding hub_rate_limits), secret (the HMAC key for the stored row id), ip (the client address, default 'local') and now (epoch milliseconds, default Date.now()). Counting is skipped and null is returned when db or secret is missing.

outputs.name: hubRateLimit
outputs.description: Resolves to null for a non-POST request, an unlisted path, a missing db or secret, or a count at or below the route cap within the current 60-second window; otherwise, including when no count row is returned, it resolves to a 429 Response from hubHttp({ error: 'rate-limited' }, 429) with a Retry-After header of 60. Caps are 5 for /api/auth/email/start, 20 for /api/auth/google, 60 for /api/auth/native/poll and 10 for the other six listed routes; counts are stored in hub_rate_limits under a hex HMAC-SHA256 digest of the IP (or 'local') and path, keyed by the secret, so no raw IP is stored.

errors.name: DOMException
errors.description: Rejects when crypto.subtle.importKey (input.secret as the HMAC key) or crypto.subtle.sign (the IP or 'local', a colon and the path) rejects; the function does not catch it, so the caller receives that rejection.

errors.name: Hub rate-limit D1 write failure
errors.description: Rejects with whatever the D1 binding rejects with when the upsert into hub_rate_limits (prepare, bind and first) fails for input.db; the function does not catch it, so the caller receives that rejection instead of a Response or null.
